title: Terroristic Threats
grade_or_penalty: Third degree under (a) or (b). Subsection (a) becomes second degree if committed during a declared national, State or county emergency.
key_points: (a) Threatening any crime of violence aimed at terrorizing someone, forcing an evacuation of a building, assembly place or transit facility, or causing serious public inconvenience.
(b) Threatening to kill someone to put them in imminent fear of death, where the circumstances would reasonably make the victim believe the threat is immediate and likely to be carried out.
Emergency upgrade is strict liability: the State only proves the emergency existed.
Reckless-disregard prosecutions under (a) are limited by State v. Fair (2024): see the related case entry.
officer_notes: Record the exact words used and how the victim reacted.
For (b), note facts showing the threat seemed immediate and likely (weapon, proximity, history).
elements: (a): The suspect threatened to commit a crime of violence
(a): With purpose to terrorize another, or to cause evacuation or serious public inconvenience (or in reckless disregard of that risk)
OR (b): The suspect threatened to kill another
(b): With purpose to put the victim in imminent fear of death, under circumstances reasonably causing the victim to believe the threat was immediate and likely to be carried out

subsections.label: a
subsections.text: Threatens a crime of violence with purpose to terrorize, or to cause evacuation of a building, place of assembly or transit, or serious public inconvenience, or in reckless disregard of that risk

subsections.label: b
subsections.text: Threatens to kill another with purpose to put them in imminent fear of death, under circumstances reasonably causing the victim to believe it
